G.name: Mass per metre
G.explain: How much one metre of section weighs. Sets the self-weight in your structure and much of the cost; steel is bought by the kilo.

h.name: Depth
h.explain: The overall depth of the section. Sets the structural depth of a floor or roof and so the storey height. Deeper section: stiffer against deflection.

b.name: Width
b.explain: The flange width. Adds to the stiffness about the weak axis and sets how much room you have for bearings and connections.

tw.name: Web thickness
tw.explain: The thickness of the vertical web. The web mainly carries shear; a thicker web resists more at supports and under point loads.

tf.name: Flange thickness
tf.explain: The thickness of the horizontal flanges. The flanges carry most of the bending moment; mind the flange thickness for bolt holes and welds.

t.name: Wall thickness
t.explain: The wall thickness of a hollow section or tube. At the same outer size a thicker wall gives more strength and stiffness, and more weight.

D.name: Outside diameter
D.explain: The outer size of a round tube. A tube is equally stiff in every direction; useful for columns and trusses.

A.name: Area
A.explain: The cross-sectional area. Sets how much axial force (tension or compression) the section can carry and, with the density, its weight.

Iy.name: Second moment of area, strong axis
Iy.explain: How stiff the section is against bending about the strong axis. Use it to estimate beam deflection: twice as large means half the deflection.

Iz.name: Second moment of area, weak axis
Iz.explain: The stiffness about the weak axis. Important for columns, which usually buckle about this axis.

Wy.name: Section modulus, strong axis
Wy.explain: Links bending moment to stress: stress = moment / W. Use it to check whether a beam is strong enough.

Wz.name: Section modulus, weak axis
Wz.explain: Like W about the strong axis, but for bending about the weak axis, for example wind on the flange.

iy.name: Radius of gyration, strong axis
iy.explain: √(I/A): how far, on average, the material lies from the axis. Needed for slenderness and so for buckling about the strong axis.

iz.name: Radius of gyration, weak axis
iz.explain: √(I/A) about the weak axis. Usually governs column buckling: smaller i, earlier buckling.

timber.title: Timber
timber.flagged: No value in the Vademecum table fits this size. The size may not belong in the table. A, W and I are still calculated exactly for a b × h rectangle.
timber.method: Sizes (b × h) from the table; A, W and I calculated exactly for a rectangle. Every table cell was checked against this calculation.

explain.A: The area of the cross-section, b × h. Sets how much tension or compression the member can carry and, with the density of the timber, the weight per metre.
explain.Wy: Section modulus about the strong axis, b·h²/6. Links bending moment to stress: stress = moment / W. Use it to check whether a beam on edge is strong enough.
explain.Iy: Second moment of area about the strong axis, b·h³/12. Says how stiff the beam is against deflection. Because h counts to the third power, a deeper beam helps far more than a wider one.
explain.Wz: Section modulus about the weak axis, h·b²/6. Matters when the member lies flat or is loaded sideways.
explain.Iz: Second moment of area about the weak axis, h·b³/12. Usually governs buckling of a stud or column, and lateral torsional buckling of slender beams.

timber.hatch: Timber hatch from the Vademecum (NEN 2302). The source gives no separate hatch for glulam.

about.title: About BARCHY
about.whyTitle: Everything you need, in your pocket
about.why: I am an architecture student. While designing I kept looking up the same data: a section table in the Vademecum, a requirement in the Bbl, a hatch in the drawing instructions. It is all out there, but scattered. BARCHY brings it together in one clear place, so it is always at hand, even offline.
about.sources: All data comes from these sources. Values are never made up: anything not yet checked is marked "Check". Every value shows its own source.
about.open: The BARCHY code is public under the MIT licence. The data follows the licence of its source: the Vademecum is CC BY 4.0. Anyone can look along, report errors or contribute.
about.reportError: Found an error? Report a correction
about.feedbackTitle: Want to add or request something?
about.feedbackIntro: Missing a table, something not right, or an idea? Let me know. Your message goes straight to the maker.
about.sent: Thank you! Your message has been sent.
about.offline: Sending only works online. Your text stays here.
about.error: Sending failed. Please try again later.
about.noForm: Share your idea or error on GitHub.
about.installBody: Open BARCHY with one tap from your home screen, even without internet. Pick your browser below.

disclaimer.title: Before you start
disclaimer.body: The information in BARCHY is taken from the TU Delft Vademecum and the Dutch Building Decree (Bbl). It may contain small errors. Always check values in the source before you use them.
disclaimer.unofficial: BARCHY is a student project, not an official TU Delft app.

dev.sampleText: Pick a section and calculate its weight right away.
dev.sampleTileBody: The second moment of area tells you how stiff a section is against bending.

stair.scope: Straight stair in a dwelling, new build. Limits from Bbl art. 4.26, table 4.26.
stair.allOk: Meets these four requirements. Also check the other requirements below.
stair.info: The calculator uses the limits from this app’s Bbl facts. It does not check clear height, walking line, landing or handrail; those are listed under Also applies.

sheets.title: Profiled steel sheets
sheets.Iy: Second moment of area per metre
sheets.flagged: The Vademecum column header gives contradictory units. Iy and Wy are read here as ×10⁴ mm⁴/m and ×10³ mm³/m, and the source does not say which stress σ is. Do not use these values without checking the source.
sheets.units: Iy and Wy per metre of sheet width, according to our reading of the column header. Not yet confirmed.

explain.h: The height of the profile, from the bottom to the top of the rib. A deeper sheet is stiffer and can span further.
explain.t: The thickness of the steel the sheet is formed from. A thicker sheet is stronger and stiffer, but also heavier.
explain.Iy: Second moment of area per metre of sheet width. Says how stiff the sheet is against deflection between supports.
explain.Wy: Section modulus per metre of sheet width. Links bending moment to stress: stress = moment / W.
explain.sigma: The source does not say which stress this is. Do not use this value until its meaning is clear.

sheets.unitNote: Unit read here as {unit}. The Vademecum column header is contradictory.
sheets.sigmaNote: Meaning and unit not explained in the source.

rules.title: Rules of thumb
rules.chartWhere: The chart itself is in the source: {ref}.
rules.flagged: These rules of thumb were copied by hand from the Vademecum and have not been checked yet. Use them for a first estimate and check the source when in doubt.
rules.method: Each column of a table in the source is one set of rules with the same range. Charts are referenced, without values read from them.
rules.diagram: Diagram drawn by BARCHY after the figure in the Vademecum.

masonry.title: Masonry
masonry.heading: Calcium silicate: minimum wall thickness
masonry.caption: Lowest storey, {n} storeys, bay width {l} m, floor thickness {ht} mm
masonry.tableCaption: Minimum structural wall thickness d in mm by number of storeys (rows) and bay width (columns)
masonry.tableNote: Rows: number of storeys. Columns: bay width in m, with the thickness hₜ of the structural floor in mm. Tap a cell to pick it.
masonry.method: Tables from the Vademecum, based on NPR 6791. The source only gives bay widths of 4, 5, 6 and 7 m.

beam.scope: Estimate the depth of a beam or frame from its span, with the rules of thumb from the Vademecum. A first estimate, not a calculation.
beam.outside: l = {l} m is outside the range of this rule of thumb ({range}). Use the estimate with care.
beam.unknown: cannot be computed from l alone; see the source figure
beam.allRules: All rules of thumb for this shape
beam.info: Depth = span / n from the rule of thumb, rounded to 10 mm. For a range (e.g. l/15 – l/20) the smallest depth goes with the largest n.
beam.legHeightHint: From the base to the knee, as in the source figure. h_knik = (l+g)/n.

install.title: Add BARCHY to your home screen
install.intro: Then you open BARCHY with one tap, like any app, and it works offline too.

ios-safari.name: iPhone or iPad (Safari)
ios-safari.s1: Tap the share button (square with an arrow pointing up) at the bottom or top.
ios-safari.s2: Scroll and choose ‘Add to Home Screen’.

ios-other.name: iPhone or iPad (Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
ios-other.s1: Tap the share button or the menu (⋯) of your browser.
ios-other.s2: Choose ‘Add to Home Screen’. Not there? Open BARCHY in Safari and follow the steps there.

android-chrome.name: Android (Chrome)
android-chrome.s1: Tap the menu at the top right (three dots).
android-chrome.s2: Choose ‘Install app’ or ‘Add to Home screen’.

android-samsung.name: Android (Samsung Internet)
android-samsung.s1: Tap the menu at the bottom (three lines).
android-samsung.s2: Choose ‘Add page to’ and then ‘Home screen’.

android-other.name: Android (other browser)
android-other.s1: Open your browser's menu (usually three dots).
android-other.s2: Choose ‘Install app’ or ‘Add to Home screen’.
android-other.s3: Does not work? Open BARCHY in Chrome.

desktop-chromium.name: Computer (Chrome, Edge)
desktop-chromium.s1: Click the install icon (monitor with an arrow) at the right of the address bar.

desktop-safari.name: Mac (Safari)
desktop-safari.s1: Click ‘Share’ or ‘File’ in the menu bar.

desktop-other.name: Computer (other browser)
desktop-other.s1: This browser cannot install BARCHY. Open it in Chrome, Edge or Safari, or bookmark it.
